Título: A Novel Framework for Smart Cyber Defence: A Deep-Dive Into Deep Learning Attacks and Defences
Autores: Arshad, Iram and Alsamhi, Saeed Hamood and Qiao, Yuansong and Lee, Brian and Ye, Yuhang
Abstract: Deep learning techniques have been widely adopted for cyber defence applications such as malware detection and anomaly detection. The ever-changing nature of cyber threats has made cyber defence a constantly evolving field. Smart manufacturing is critical to the broader thrust towards Industry 4.0 and 5.0. Developing advanced technologies in smart manufacturing requires enabling a paradigm shift in manufacturing, while cyber-attacks significantly threaten smart manufacturing. For example, a cyber attack (e.g., backdoor) occurs during the model’s training process. Cyber attack affects the models and impacts the resultant output to be misled. Therefore, this paper proposes a novel and comprehensive framework for smart cyber defence in deep learning security. The framework collectively incorporates a threat model, data, and model security. The proposed framework encompasses multiple layers, including privacy and protection of data and models. In addition to statistical and intelligent model techniques for maintaining data privacy and confidentiality, the proposed framework covers the structural perspective, i.e., policies and procedures for securing data. The study then offers different methods to make the models robust against attacks coupled with a threat model. Along with the model security, the threat model helps defend the smart systems against attacks by identifying potential or actual vulnerabilities and putting countermeasures and control in place. Moreover, based on our analysis, the study provides a taxonomy of the backdoor attacks and defences. In addition, the study provides a qualitative comparison of the existing backdoor attacks and defences. Finally, the study highlights the future directions for backdoor defences and provides a possible way for further research.
Keywords: Security;Data models;Threat modeling;Training;Cyberattack;Toxicology;Industries;Deep learning;Smart devices;Backdoor attacks;cyber-attacks;deep learning;defences;security;smart cyber defence;smart manufacturing security

Título: Cyber Attacks via Consumer Electronics: Studying the Threat of Covert Malware in Smart and Autonomous Vehicles
Autores: Sayad Haghighi, Mohammad and Farivar, Faezeh and Jolfaei, Alireza and Asl, Azin Bayrami and Zhou, Wei
Abstract: In Industry 5.0, man and machine work alongside each other in production, but smart and autonomous vehicles are examples that show this notion is now being extended to the end consumers. In 2015, a Jeep was remotely hacked through its head unit. This incident drew the public attention to vehicles security and showed how entertainment/infotainment consumer electronics can be used to intrude vehicles. In this paper, we study a novel covert attack that can be launched by malwares spreading through Intelligent Transportation Systems, e.g., via consumer electronics. This malware infects a vehicle module, like the Adaptive Cruise Controller (ACC), and manipulates its setting in a way that is not noticeable to human observers, but gives rise to accidents statistics. We show how this is done and analyze the effect mathematically. We also propose a new Intrusion Detection System (IDS) whose architecture is non-disruptive and can be readily adopted by car manufacturers. We evaluate our proposal with real-world datasets. We demonstrate how a malware/attacker can engineer the crash statistics by manipulating the safe distance value in cruise control scenarios. Then, we put an anomaly-based IDS for ACC modules into test and show how it can effectively detect such covert attacks.
Keywords: Cyberattack;Malware;Cruise control;Connected vehicles;Autonomous vehicles;Consumer electronics;Fifth Industrial Revolution;Intelligent transportation systems;Cruise control;Security;Intrusion detection;Consumer electronics;industry 5.0;intelligent transportation systems;adaptive cruise control;security;worm;intrusion detection system

Título: A Linear Probabilistic Resilience Model for Securing Critical Infrastructure in Industry 5.0
Autores: Abuhasel, Khaled Ali
Abstract: Critical infrastructures are designed for securing interconnecting networks from different influencing factors such as adversaries, unauthorized platoons, cyber threats, etc. These infrastructure hosts include human, physical elements, and cyber paradigms. The vital part is cyber resilience against weak and volatile authentication and security administrations. For strengthening cyber security, this article introduces the Artificial Intelligence-induced Constructive Resilience Model (AI-CRM). The proposed model accounts for the security requirements of the adversary impacting infrastructure elements based on probability. This probability is computed using previous adversary impacts on infrastructure failures and session drops in handling operational services. The computation for linearity or stagnancy is validated using a recurrent learning paradigm over different service transitions. The resilience is improved by augmenting security measures that are identified as an output of linear impacts over the services. Based on the linear incremental probability the resilience between two successive service transitions is computed. Identifying the non-linear or stagnant probability is the converging solution of recurrent learning. The recurrent learning optimizes the stagnancy and linear impact (probability) by repeatedly computing the failures and drops due to adversary injection. This improves resilience through security augmentations and modifications. This model is analyzed using adversary detection ratio, session drops, infrastructure failures, time lag, and service dissemination ratio.
Keywords: Security;Resilience;Critical infrastructure;Computational modeling;Task analysis;Feature extraction;Recurrent neural networks;Critical infrastructure;Learning systems;Critical infrastructure;linear processing;recurrent learning;resilience

Título: Steps Toward Industry 5.0: Building “6S” Parallel Industries With Cyber-Physical-Social Intelligence
Autores: Wang, Xingxia and Yang, Jing and Wang, Yutong and Miao, Qinghai and Wang, Fei-Yue and Zhao, Aijun and Deng, Jian-Ling and Li, Lingxi and Na, Xiaoxiang and Vlacic, Ljubo
Abstract: Very recently, intensive discussions and studies on Industry 5.0 have sprung up and caused the attention of researchers, entrepreneurs, and policymakers from various sectors around the world. However, there is no consensus on why and what is Industry 5.0 yet. In this paper, we define Industry 5.0 from its philosophical and historical origin and evolution, emphasize its new thinking on virtual-real duality and human-machine interaction, and introduce its new theory and technology based on parallel intelligence (PI), artificial societies, computational experiments, and parallel execution (the ACP method), and cyber-physical-social systems (CPSS). Case studies and applications of Industry 5.0 over the last decade have been briefly summarized and analyzed with suggestions for its future development. We believe that Industry 5.0 of virtual-real interactive parallel industries has great potentials and is critical for building smart societies. Steps are outlined to ensure a roadmap that would lead to a smooth transition from CPS-based Industry 4.0 to CPSS-based Industry 5.0 for a better world which is Safe in physical spaces, Secure in cyberspaces, Sustainable in ecology, Sensitive in indi-vidual privacy and rights, Service for all, and Smartness of all.
Keywords: Industries;Privacy;Service robots;Robot kinematics;Buildings;Smart contracts;Transportation;ACP;artificial intelligence;CPS;CPSS;Industry 4.0;Industry 5.0;parallel industries;parallel intelligence

Título: Microservice Deployment Mechanism With Diversified QoS Requirements for Smart Health System in Industry 5.0
Autores: Zhang, Hong and Luo, Jun and Tu, Yanli and Wang, Ruyan and Wu, Dapeng and Yang, Jing
Abstract: By collecting and processing smart healthcare data in real-time, mobile edge networks can bridge the gap between doctors and patients, which is a representative consumer-level data interaction scenario in Industry 5.0. To improve the flexibility and timeliness of suchlike Industry 5.0 services, microservices are deployed extensively on edge servers. The major challenge facing microservice deployment is how to reduce the cost. However, cost and quality of service (QoS) are a pair of contradictory objectives, and different scenarios have different preferences for the two objectives, which is easy to be ignored. In order to solve this problem, this paper considers service responsiveness and user mobility in the response process of requests. Then a Constrained Multi-objective Optimization Problem (CMOP) is formulated by combining deployment cost and task completion rate. Considering the differentiated requirements of users in different scenarios, this paper proposes a Multi-objective Optimization Evolutionary Algorithm with the Penalty Mechanism (MOEA-PM) to solve this CMOP. Simulation results demonstrate that adding a penalty segment to the fitness function can boost algorithm efficiency significantly. Compared with baseline algorithms, MOEA-PM always yields a microservice deployment strategy set adapted to a variety of industry 5.0 scenarios.
Keywords: Microservice architectures;Medical services;Quality of service;Fifth Industrial Revolution;Smart healthcare;Multi-access edge computing;Optimization;Industry 5.0;smart healthcare;mobile edge network;microservice deployment;multi-objective optimization

Título: Retracted: Logistics 5.0: From Intelligent Networks to Sustainable Ecosystems
Autores: Li, Juanjuan and Qin, Rui and Olaverri-Monreal, Cristina and Prodan, Radu and Wang, Fei-Yue
Abstract: As part of TIV's DHW on Vehicle 5.0, this letter introduces a novel concept, Logistics 5.0, to address high complexities in logistics Cyber-Physical-Social Systems (CPSS). Building upon the theory of parallel intelligence and leveraging advanced technologies and methods such as blockchain, scenarios engineering, Decentralized Autonomous Organizations and Operations (DAOs), Logistics 5.0 promises to accelerate the paradigm shift towards intelligent and sustainable logistics. First, the parallel logistics framework is proposed, and the logistics ecosystem is discussed. Then, the human-oriented operating systems (HOOS) are suggested to providing intelligent Logistics 5.0 solutions. Logistics 5.0 serves as a critical catalyst in realizing the “6S” objectives, i.e. Safety, Security, Sustainability, Sensitivity, Service, and Smartness, within the logistics industry.

Título: Enabling Efficient Data Integration of Industry 5.0 Nodes Through Highly Accurate Neural CSI Feedback
Autores: Hussien, Mostafa and Nguyen, Kim Khoa and Ranjha, Ali and Krichen, Moez and Alshammari, Abdulaziz and Cheriet, Mohamed
Abstract: Industry 5.0 refers to the fifth industrial revolution that leverages advanced technologies such as Internet of things (IoT) and artificial intelligence (AI) to increase efficiency, productivity, and flexibility in manufacturing and other industries. Wireless IoT devices help collect and transmit real-time data to support intelligent decision-making, while AI algorithms process and analyze the data to optimize production processes, predict equipment failure, and enhance supply chain management. To achieve efficient integration for the data fused by various sensors, the data should be perfectly synchronized and out-of-errors. In cellular-based sensors, this requires the base station (BS) to know the state of the channel at each node. In this work, we propose a novel method for CSI compression by learning an approximation for a sufficient statistics function. Our method establishes a new category of compression techniques based on the theory of sufficient statistics. Moreover, we present a detailed analysis of the upper bound of the prediction error in our specific scenario. We develop a Bayesian optimization framework to optimally select the adopted neural network architecture. The experimental results confirm that our solution outperforms both conventional and learning-based solutions in terms of reconstruction error, model size, and scalability.
Keywords: 5G mobile communication;Internet of Things;Artificial intelligence;MIMO communication;Data integration;Fifth Industrial Revolution;Channel state information;Industry 50;data integration;CSI compression

Título: Healthcare 5.0: In the Perspective of Consumer Internet-of-Things-Based Fog/Cloud Computing
Autores: Chi, Hao Ran and de Fátima Domingues, Maria and Zhu, Hongxu and Li, Chunguo and Kojima, Kazuyuki and Radwan, Ayman
Abstract: Nowadays, our society has been experiencing the development of Healthcare 4.0, focusing on digitalization by utilizing cloud/fog computing-based consumer Internet-of-Things (CIoT). Meanwhile, Industry 5.0 has been defined recently, targeting improving the current Industry 4.0. Inspired by Industry 5.0, we are among the first wave of researchers to propose Healthcare 5.0, specifically in the perspective of fog/cloud computing. Concretely, we perform a comprehensive vertical and horizontal summary of Healthcare 1.0 – 4.0 and Industry 1.0 – 4.0, which enables us to be among the first research efforts to provide a unique prediction of the corresponding upcoming Healthcare 5.0, based on Industry 5.0. In particular, we predict the potential development in Healthcare 5.0, specifically for fog/cloud computing, on top of a comprehensive overview of the role and state-of-the-art development in Healthcare 4.0. We also give our unique insight of the potential technologies of CIoT and fog/cloud computing in Healthcare 5.0, as well as the corresponding opportunities and challenges. Therefore, for the first time, this article provides deep and well-thought insight to open a new era towards the future fog/cloud computing for healthcare system development towards Healthcare 5.0.

Título: Heart Rate Variability Measurement to Assess Acute Work-Content-Related Stress of Workers in Industrial Manufacturing Environment—A Systematic Scoping Review
Autores: Tran, Tuan-Anh and Péntek, Márta and Motahari-Nezhad, Hossein and Abonyi, János and Kovács, Levente and Gulácsi, László and Eigner, György and Zrubka, Zsombor and Ruppert, Tamás
Jornal/Conferência: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man, and Cybernetics: Systems
Abstract: Background: Human workers are indispensable in the human–cyber-physical system in the forthcoming Industry 5.0. As inappropriate work content induces stress and harmful effects on human performance, engineering applications search for a physiological indicator for monitoring the well-being state of workers during work; thus, the work content can be modified accordingly. The primary aim of this study is to assess whether heart rate variability (HRV) can be a valid and reliable indicator of acute work-content-related stress (AWCRS) in real time during industrial work. Second, we aim to provide a broader scope of HRV usage as a stress indicator in this context. Methods: A search was conducted in Scopus, IEEE Xplore, PubMed, and Web of Science between 1 January 2000 and 1 June 2022. Eligible articles are analyzed regarding study design, population, assessment of AWCRS, and its association with HRV. Results: A total of 14 studies met the inclusion criteria. No randomized control trial (RCT) was conducted to assess the association between AWCRS and HRV. Five observational studies were performed. Both AWCRS and HRV were measured in nine further studies, but their associations were not analyzed. Results suggest that HRV does not fully reflect the AWCRS during work, and it is problematic to measure the effect of AWCRS on HRV in the real manufacturing environment. The evidence is insufficient for a reliable conclusion about the HRV diagnostic role as an indicator of human worker status. Conclusion: This review is valuable in the Operator 4.0 paradigm, calling for more trials to validate the use of HRV to measure AWCRS on human workers.
Keywords: Heart rate variability;Human factors;Stress;Stress measurement;Manufacturing;Biomedical monitoring;Monitoring;Heart rate variability (HRV);human–cyber-physical system (H-CPS);Industry 50;Operator 40;stress;systematic literature review

Título: AoI Violation Constrained Control Cost Optimization for Delay-Sensitive Industrial IoT
Autores: Su, Jiawei and Liu, Zhixin and Li, Yaping and Yuan, Yazhou and Ma, Kai
Abstract: Dear Editor, The industrial internet of things (IIoT) integrates communications and controls into a cohesive system within the framework of Industry 5.0, where time delay critically impairs system performance. Especially, the introduction of wireless networks results in more severe induced delays than wired networks, owing to the greater complexity of factors affecting reliable state updates. From the perspective of control requirements, the state update process depends on the successful rate and real-time performance of information transmission. A low successful transmission rate causes data backlog and delays state updates, while a high rate reduces delay but requires more communication resources. Nevertheless, the control center must rely on previously updated state information before the next sampling period. Therefore, simply increasing the transmission rate may not necessarily enhance long-term system performance.

Título: Input-Output Data Driven Intelligent $H_\infty$ Fault-Tolerant Tracking Control for Industrial Process in Industry 5.0
Autores: Wang, Limin and Jia, Linzhu and Zhang, Ridong
Abstract: Dear Editor, This letter investigates a data-driven $H_{\infty}$ feedback fault-tolerant tracking control problem using off-policy Q-learning, focusing on challenges such as unobservable system states, external disturbances, and actuator faults in industrial processes. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through simulations on an injection molding process.

Título: Event-Triggered Adaptive Control of Noncanonical Nonlinear Systems with Hysteresis Inputs
Autores: Lai, Guanyu and Zeng, Kairong and Wang, Yonghua and Zhang, Tao and Xiao, Hanzhen
Abstract: Dear Editor, It is well known that event-triggered control (ETC) is an effective approach in addressing networked control problems for Industry 5.0. Its feasibility, however, is still restricted to canonical nonlinear systems so far. Considering this, a gradient-based adaptive ETC scheme for noncanonical nonlinear systems is newly developed in this letter, where the hysteresis input constraints are considered also. By proper decomposition, the technical issue of handling ETC-induced measurement errors and hysteresis inputs can be transformed into the robustness problem to bounded disturbance-like terms, which is then addressed by integrating a switching modification strategy in adaptive design and developing a novel augmented error-based analysis framework. Experimental results based on a practical piezoactuator confirm the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

Título: Editorial SI on Advances in AI for 6G Networks
Autores: Chergui, Hatim and Tourki, Kamel and Wu, Jun
Abstract: The advent of 6G networks heralds a new era of telecommunications characterized by unparalleled connectivity, ultra-low latency, and immersive applications such as holographic communication and Industry 5.0. However, these advancements also introduce significant complexities in network management and service orchestration. This Special Issue of IEEE Networking Letters explores cutting-edge research on Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven automation techniques designed to address these challenges. The selected works span a diverse array of AI paradigms—ranging from generative AI (GenAI) and reinforcement learning to multi-agent systems and federated learning—showcasing their applications across various 6G technological domains. By highlighting these innovations, this issue aims to provide valuable insights into the pivotal role of AI in shaping the future of 6G networks.
Keywords: Special issues and sections;Artificial intelligence;6G mobile communication;Generative AI

Título: Retraction Notice: Logistics 5.0: From Intelligent Networks to Sustainable Ecosystems
Autores: Li, Juanjuan and Qin, Rui and Olaverri-Monreal, Cristina and Prodan, Radu and Wang, Fei-Yue
Abstract: As part of TIV's DHW on Vehicle 5.0, this letter introduces a novel concept, Logistics 5.0, to address high complexities in logistics Cyber-Physical-Social Systems (CPSS). Building upon the theory of parallel intelligence and leveraging advanced technologies and methods such as blockchain, scenarios engineering, Decentralized Autonomous Organizations and Operations (DAOs), Logistics 5.0 promises to accelerate the paradigm shift towards intelligent and sustainable logistics. First, the parallel logistics framework is proposed, and the logistics ecosystem is discussed. Then, the human-oriented operating systems (HOOS) are suggested to providing intelligent Logistics 5.0 solutions. Logistics 5.0 serves as a critical catalyst in realizing the “6S” objectives, i.e. Safety, Security, Sustainability, Sensitivity, Service, and Smartness, within the logistics industry.

Abstract: The logistics and transportation industry has made significant progress in improving sustainability, efficiency, and accessibility, primarily due to the continuous development of technologies, including clean energy, advanced algorithms, unmanned vehicles, and privacy-enhancing techniques. By integrating emerging technologies into Cyber-Physical-Social Systems (CPSS), we believe that Mobility 5.0 has tremendous potential in shaping a new era of intelligent logistics and transportation services and will bring significant benefits to individuals, businesses, the government, and the entire society.

Abstract: In recent years, the integration of advanced technologies such as communication advancements (e.g., 5G), Artificial Intelligence (AI), industrial edge computing, and adversarial Machine Learning (ML) has accelerated the evolution of Industry 5.0 systems, shaping digital ecosystems for consumers. This convergence of technologies holds promise for addressing the service requirements and cybersecurity strategies essential for Industry 5.0 systems within digital ecosystems. Industry 5.0, the fifth industrial revolution, represents a paradigm shift integrating digital ecosystems and emerging technologies like the Internet of Things (IoT), Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS), cloud computing, and AI. Título: Automation 5.0: The Key to Systems Intelligence and Industry 5.0
Autores: Vlacic, Ljubo and Huang, Hailong and Dotoli, Mariagrazia and Wang, Yutong and Ioannou, Petros A. and Fan, Lili and Wang, Xingxia and Carli, Raffaele and Lv, Chen and Li, Lingxi and Na, Xiaoxiang and Han, Qing-Long and Wang, Fei-Yue
Abstract: Automation has come a long way since the early days of mechanization, i.e., the process of working exclusively by hand or using animals to work with machinery. The rise of steam engines and water wheels represented the first generation of industry, which is now called Industry 1.0. Subsequently, Industry 2.0 witnessed the development of electric power and assembly lines. Later on, programmable logic controllers and Human Machine Interfaces (HMI) were the new productivity tools in Industry 3.0, which enabled precise and consistent production. In recent years, Industry 4.0 absorbed the latest technologies of Internet of Things (IoT), Artificial Intelligence (AI), and big data, making production processes integrated, interconnected, and smart. Nowadays, Industry 5.0 has been proposed, which emphasizes human-centric automation. Specifically, the new concept of automation in Industry 5.0, named Automation 5.0, is no longer about how to create machinery to replace humans. Instead, it aims to reach organic interactions and cooperation between humans and machines, meeting the goal of “6S” - Safety, Security, Sustainability, Sensitivity, Service, and Smartness [1]–[4] - and the overall objective of deploying automation for the better, human-friendly, and smarter industry.

This collaboration aims to increase consumer value while improving industrial automation. Industry 5.0 focuses more on cooperation than competition. Personalized services are provided by linking data from various sensors to highlight distinct product characteristics based on consumer preferences. A high-tech strategy uses the Internet of Things to provide industrial automation along with personalized consumer services through symmetric innovation via democratized Big Data knowledge.

Título: Parallel Factories for Smart Industrial Operations: From Big AI Models to Field Foundational Models and Scenarios Engineering
Autores: Lu, Jingwei and Wang, Xingxia and Cheng, Xiang and Yang, Jing and Kwan, Oliver and Wang, Xiao
Abstract: Briefing: The rapid advancement of fundamental theories and computing capacity has brought artificial intelligence, internet of things, extended reality, and many other new intelligent technologies into our daily lives. Due to the lack of interpretability and reliability guarantees, it is extremely challenging to apply these technologies directly to real-world industrial systems. Here we present a new paradigm for establishing parallel factories in metaverses to accelerate the deployment of intelligent technologies in real-world industrial systems: QAII-1.0. Based on cyber-physical-social systems, QAII-1.0 incorporates complex social and human factors into the design and analysis of industrial operations and is capable of handling industrial operations involving complex social and human behaviors. In QAII-1.0, a field foundational model called EuArtisan combined with scenarios engineering is developed to improve the intelligence of industrial systems while ensuring industrial interpretability and reliability. Finally, parallel oil fields in metaverses are established to demonstrate the operating procedure of QAII-1.0.

Título: Co-Design of Control, Energy, and Buffer with Delay Determinism for Consumer Electronics in Industry 5.0
Autores: Feng, Lei and Cao, Yalin and Yang, Zhixiang and Li, Ying and Zhang, Qiyang and Zhou, Fanqin and Zhou, Lijie and Wei, Lei
Abstract: The deployment of wireless control systems in consumer electronics (CEs) is one of the critical components in Industry 5.0 to enable real-time monitoring and control with efficiency, flexibility, and reliability. This paper presents a novel model for the co-design of control, energy, and buffer management with delay determinism for CEs in Industry 5.0. To tackle the non-convex problem of minimizing long-term average joint cost, we propose an efficient resource allocation mechanism based on Lyapunov optimization theory and alternating optimization, utilizing control state information feedback. Specifically, the long-term problem is equivalently converted into an instantaneous optimization problem, which is then decomposed into two iteratively solvable subproblems, namely the buffer allocation problem and the bandwidth allocation problem. The subproblems are solved by branch and bound method and the interior point method, respectively. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed mechanism outperforms four baseline mechanisms, achieving a balance between delay determinism, control stability, and efficient resource utilization.
Keywords: Delays;Control systems;Wireless communication;Resource management;Optimization;Costs;Stability analysis;Fifth Industrial Revolution;Bandwidth;Consumer electronics;Industry 5.0;Consumer electronics;Wireless control system;Lyapunov optimization

Título: Task-Oriented Network Reliability for Federated Learning-Enabled Industrial Internet of Things
Autores: Zheng, Dingyi and Fu, Xiuwen and Pace, Pasquale and Aloi, Gianluca and Fortino, Giancarlo
Abstract: With the rapid development of Industry 5.0, the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) plays an increasingly important role as a key information infrastructure supporting data collection, transmission, and decision-making. Federated Learning-enabled IIoT (FL-enabled IIoT) systems deploy artificial intelligence (AI) models at the network edge and utilize model aggregation mechanisms to facilitate efficient data processing and intelligent decision-making. However, anomalies occurring in local nodes can propagate through the aggregation process, leading to model contamination and performance degradation, thereby compromising overall system reliability. To address this issue, this paper proposes a reliability model for FL-enabled IIoT systems. In this model, we systematically describe the entire process of model performance degradation caused by node failures and its impact on system task reliability. This includes the effects of multiple functional failures induced by node faults (i.e., data loss, communication interruption, and computational resource degradation) on model performance, as well as the failure propagation process caused by model contamination and data quality deterioration. Additionally, to evaluate the impact of model performance variations on practical production tasks, a task-oriented reliability metric is proposed. Simulation and experimental results demonstrate that the proposed modeling approach effectively characterizes the model performance degradation process and task reliability under node failure conditions.
Keywords: Reliability;Industrial Internet of Things;Computational modeling;Data models;Production;Degradation;Artificial intelligence;Collaboration;Sensors;Measurement;Federated Learning;Industrial Internet of Things;Reliability Modeling;Artificial Intelligence

Título: Unleashing the Potential of Industrial IoT and Industry 5.0
Autores: Maurya, Poonam and Hazra, Abhishek and Kalita, Alakesh
Abstract: The transition to Industry 5.0 emphasizes the need and importance of human–machine collaboration, driving the demand for intelligent Internet of Things (IoT) and communication protocols. This paper examines the essential prerequisites for Industry 5.0, evaluates the existing constraints of IoT communication protocols, and highlights the requirements for industrial convergence. Specifically, the article focuses on and discusses the role of IoT protocols and standards in realizing the key objectives of Industry 5.0 over Industry 4.0. In addition, it outlines a human-centric Industry 5.0 reference architecture designed to support managers and decision-makers through real-time data visibility, predictive maintenance insights, and resource optimization. To this end, we introduce an edge-enabled Industry 5.0 reference architecture and use cases, particularly emphasizing the enhancement of human–machine interaction. This paper also examines the 6TiSCH (IPv6 over the Time-Slotted Channel Hopping mode of IEEE 802.15.4e) wireless network protocol, focusing on its performance evaluation, prospective advantages, and upcoming advancements. Finally, several open research challenges and managerial implications are discussed to achieve Industry 5.0 resolution.
Keywords: Fifth Industrial Revolution;Protocols;Fourth Industrial Revolution;Collaboration;Industries;Decision making;Creativity;Robots;Resilience;Industrial Internet of Things;Industry 5.0;Internet of Things;standards & protocols

Título: From Sensing to Segmentation: Transformer-Based Worker Activity Recognition for Industrial Assembly
Autores: Sbaragli, Andrea and Nardello, Matteo
Abstract: Human operators still provide strategic, value-added contributions to modern manufacturing systems, despite the widespread adoption of automation. This paper presents a cyber-physical system designed to perform fine-grained Worker Activity Recognition (WAR) and segment manual operations in human-centric assembly environments. The proposed system includes a modular and low-intrusion IoT acquisition layer that digitizes worker movements using Inertial Measurement Units (IMUs) and a radio frequency-based smart glove. While the IMUs track hand and back motion, the glove captures process interactions such as picking and depositing components. These multimodal data streams are processed by a cyber layer that performs time- and frequency-domain feature extraction and feeds the data into a Transformer-based neural network to classify five common assembly tasks. The results are post-processed by a Decision Support System to generate interpretable task segments and provide key performance indicators for industrial supervisors. The system is validated through a real-world deployment involving three workers assembling a vertical centrifugal pump, resulting in over 7 hours of annotated data. The Transformer model achieves an F1-score of 82% on this dataset. Thanks to its unobtrusive sensors, low deployment cost, and robustness to occlusions, the proposed solution offers a practical and scalable approach to enhancing visibility and traceability in manual industrial operations.
Keywords: Assembly;Accuracy;Activity recognition;Feature extraction;Transformers;Sensors;Manufacturing;Hands;Decision support systems;Motion segmentation;Human-centric manufacturing;industry 5.0;IoT;CPS;machine learning;worker activity recognition

Título: Optimization of Circular Disassembly Lines With Human-Assisted Robotic Workstations Using Two-Stage Greedy PPO Algorithm
Autores: Qin, Shujin and Feng, Yujie and Wang, Jiacun and Liu, Shixin and Guo, Xiwang and Qi, Liang
Jornal/Conferência: IEEE Transactions on Computational Social Systems
Abstract: Disassembly is a critical step in the recycling and reusing of end-of-life products. As Industry 5.0 emerges, manufacturing is shifting from a system-oriented approach to a human-centered paradigm, advancing human–robot collaboration to a new stage. However, existing studies on human–robot collaboration in disassembly lines generally overlook the mobility of workers. To fill the research gap, this work proposes a novel human–robot collaboration mode that considers both the mobility of workers during disassembly and the flexibility of collaboration time in human–robot interaction. Based on this model, this work proposes the human-assisted robotic circular disassembly line balancing problem and establishes a profit-oriented spatiotemporal decomposition mixed-integer programming model. A two-stage greedy proximal policy optimization algorithm is designed to solve it. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed model and algorithm, ten sets of benchmark instances are generated with different scales based on real product structure data. Comparative experiments with reinforcement learning algorithms and classical heuristic methods demonstrate the feasibility and significant superiority of the proposed algorithm in solving this type of problem.
Keywords: Collaboration;Workstations;Optimization;Heuristic algorithms;Recycling;Service robots;Mathematical models;Electronic waste;Spatiotemporal phenomena;Production;Circular disassembly line;human-assisted robotic disassembly;spatiotemporal decomposition method;two-stage greedy PPO (TSG-PPO) algorithm

Título: Machine Learning-Based Early Detection of Sarcopenia-prone Risk Using Five-Time Sit-to-Stand Test Analysis
Autores: Wang, Keer and Zhang, Hongyu and Chen, Meng and Lai, King Wai Chiu and Or, Calvin Kalun and Hu, Yong and Vellaisamy, Arul Lenus Roy and Lam, Cindy Lo Kuen and Xi, Ning and Lou, Vivian Weiqun and Li, Wen Jung
Abstract: Sarcopenia, characterized by progressive loss of muscle mass and function, significantly impacts the quality of life in aging populations. Early detection and personalized intervention are crucial yet challenging due to the limited accessibility and scalability of traditional diagnostic methods. Building upon our previous work on gait-based assessment, this study presents a novel framework for early sarcopenia-prone risk detection using the Five-Time Sit-to-Stand Test (5TSTS), embodying Healthcare Industry 5.0’s vision of mass personalization with human-centered technology. Utilizing Internet-of-Things (IoT)-enabled wearable inertial measurement units (IMUs) and advanced analytics, our system segments 5TSTS into four biomechanically significant sub-motions (Standing Up, Standing Transition, Sitting Down, and Sitting Transition). This granular segmentation allows mass personalization in diagnostic evaluations by capturing individual-specific biomechanical profiles via wavelet-based feature extraction and machine learning techniques. Our framework employs big data analytics tools, including the eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost)-based feature selection and Support Vector Machine Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SVMSMOTE), to handle class imbalance and optimize individualized predictive accuracy. Tested on data from 52 elderly participants (aged 65-84 years), the system achieves outstanding personalized classification accuracy—up to 97.97% for multi-class risk stratification and 99.28% for binary (Healthy vs. Sarcopenia-prone) classification—highlighting its potential for precise, patient-specific clinical decision-making. Furthermore, the wireless capability of our IoT-enabled wearable IMUs, coupled with minimal setup requirements, facilitates seamless data integration into cloud-based healthcare systems. This integration supports real-time remote monitoring and personalized health management. By leveraging advanced sensing, analytics, and connectivity technologies, our approach significantly advances personalized, accessible, and scalable sarcopenia-prone risk assessment, thereby contributing directly to the vision of Healthcare Industry 5.0.
Keywords: Sensors;Muscles;Medical services;Feature extraction;Biomechanics;Accuracy;Wearable sensors;Risk management;Older adults;Legged locomotion;Sarcopenia;Five-time sit-to-stand;Wearable sensors;Machine learning;Wavelet transform;Motion analysis

Título: AQCSA: Anti-Quantum Cross-Server Authentication Protocol for the Industrial Internet of Drones
Autores: Le, Tuan-Vinh
Abstract: With the advent of Industry 5.0, humans will again take center stage in decision-making processes, fully supported by artificial intelligence (AI). Drone technology has been adopted in the industry to permit efficient monitoring, detection, and avoidance of hazardous regions during industrial processes. It gives rise to a network architecture, namely industrial internet of drones (IIoD), that is controlled and managed by human expertise. Collaborative IIoD services are conducted by two or more parties in different domains, e.g., mining, construction, etc. Since the communications are carried out via public network channels, privacy and security issues, especially the risks of quantum computing, are of utmost importance. Existing cryptographic approaches encounter several disadvantages, e.g., security vulnerabilities, poor usability, etc. Moreover, no user authentication mechanisms in the literature could provide a countermeasure to quantum attacks for the above communication. Based on lattice-based cryptography (LBC), this paper proposes an anti-quantum cross-server authentication (AQCSA) protocol for securing cross-domain communication of the collaborative services. Our work is designed with a multi-factor authentication mechanism to protect cross-server user-to-user (CS-U2U) and cross-server user-to-drone (CS-U2D) communications. We conduct some practical implementations and experiments to evaluate the security and efficiency of the AQCSA. It is proven that the protocol can withstand various attacks while achieving a reasonable implementation cost in CS-IIoD environments.
Keywords: Authentication;Protocols;Security;Drones;Cryptography;Artificial intelligence;Quantum computing;Smart cards;Proposals;Industrial Internet of Things;Industry 5.0;Industrial Internet of Drones (IIoD);Cross-Domain Communication;Collaborative Services;Lattice-Based Cryptography (LBC);Lightweight Computation;Multi-Factor Authentication

Título: Glocal-HAD: Hybrid Attention Decoder for Reconstruction-Based Vision Anomaly Detection Framework
Autores: Ishtiaq, Mariam and Won, Jongun
Abstract: Industry 5.0 has garnered significant research interest to address ill-posed automation challenges, such as vision-based anomaly detection (VAD). This is largely because the heterogeneous nature of anomalies renders the development of multiclass and multiscale VAD challenging. Although models based on transformer architecture have delivered state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance, they struggle with broader context feature fusion and maintaining a balance between anomaly detection, localization and computation cost. To fill this research gap, we propose a reconstruction-based anomaly detection framework that utilizes a global and local attention driven hybrid attention decoder termed Glocal-HAD. The proposed pipeline uses: 1) DINOv2 encoder for feature extraction, 2) a regularized multilayer perceptron (MLP) for latent feature compression, and 3) Glocal-HAD. The proposed decoder applies linear attention (LA) with associative key-value (KV) aggregation for global context and masked self attention (SA) with a constant drop rate for efficient local context. Four variants of HAD with stacked and interleaved settings of SA and LA layers are evaluated using two benchmark datasets: MVTec-AD and VisA. Using extensive ablation experiments, we conclude that for VAD, global context must inform local refinement, since models with global attention first, perform better. The proposed pipeline with Glocal-HAD achieves 99.5% anomaly classification (I-AUROC) and 98.2% anomaly localization (P-AUROC) performance on MVTec-AD, and 98.5% each (I-AUROC and P-AUROC) on the more challenging VisA dataset. To evaluate the model’s balance between accuracy and efficiency, we propose a novel metric, performance evaluation score (PES). Additionally, we share interesting open research problems related to model parameterization and regularization.
Keywords: Anomaly detection;Feature extraction;Image reconstruction;Decoding;Location awareness;Transformers;Computational modeling;Training;Costs;Computer architecture;Attention-guided localization;foundation model;hybrid attention;industrial anomaly detection;multiclass unified anomaly detection;multiscale feature fusion;reconstruction-based anomaly detection;unsupervised learning;vision anomaly detection

Título: Cognitive Control Units in Smart Manufacturing: Insights From a Soar-Based Assistance System
Autores: Precup, Stefan-Alexandru and Pirvu, Bogdan-Constantin and Gellert, Arpad and Zamfirescu, Constantin-Bala
Abstract: The growing complexity of industrial assembly processes calls for innovative, user-centered solutions, and in recent years, the adoption of assistive systems to support manual assembly tasks has attracted increasing attention. This work investigates the use of Cognitive Control Units, powered by the Soar cognitive architecture, as assistive systems in smart manufacturing. The Cognitive Control Unit has been integrated into an assembly station that can adapt itself and its processes to the user currently utilizing the station. An experimental study was conducted to evaluate the station’s effectiveness by comparing it with a previous experiment in which no guidance was provided. The findings reveal both shorter mean completion times and higher-quality assembly performance. Furthermore, participants indicated that the use of the station had a positive influence on their emotional state.

Título: DCD-Net: Dense Component Detection Network for Printed Circuit Board Assembly Inspection
Autores: Ling, Qin and Kai, Cui and Wenyuan, Zhang
Abstract: Electronic components in the printed circuit board assembly (PCBA) exhibit great diversities in categories, visual appearances and geometric dimensions. Efficient and precise detection for dense components is crucial and challenging for early quality inspection. Therefore, this paper proposes a novel dense component detection network (DCD-Net) established on a few improvements upon YOLO11-nano. First, a novel lighter GFConv block integrating Ghost convolution and a channel fusion operation is built to downsize the model, meanwhile enhancing the detection precision. Second, a creative C3DS module incorporating dynamic snake convolution is designed for excellent adaptability to diverse geometric forms and the large-scale variance of electronic components. Finally, FC-IoU loss involving the hard-easy sample distribution is proposed to facilitate the bounding box regression, boosting the positioning accuracy. The experiment results verify that the proposed DCD-Net achieves remarkable mean average precision of 91.6% (mAP@0.5) and 77.9% (mAP@0.5:0.95), exceeding 0.9% and 2.4% increments separately than YOLO11-nano. In addition, a 93 frames/s inference speed is achieved for inputs with  $640\times 640$  pixel resolution, demonstrating its notable potential to realize real-time industry applications. The code is available at https://github.com/lqin0818/DCD-Net/tree/master

Título: Neuroadaptive Fixed-Time Containment Tracking of Networked Agent Systems for Industry 5.0
Autores: Li, Weihao and Shi, Mengji and Han, Chenglin and Lin, Boxian and Qin, Kaiyu
Abstract: In the era of Industry 5.0, achieving rapid and robust coordination in networked agent systems (NASs) is essential for enabling intelligent collaborative autonomy. To this end, this paper investigates the distributed fixed-time containment tracking problem for NASs subject to input saturation and lumped uncertainties. A novel fixed-time extended state observer (FxTESO) is first proposed to estimate uncertain leader dynamics without requiring prior knowledge of system bounds. Then, a neural network-based adaptive estimator is developed to compensate for unknown model uncertainties and external disturbances affecting follower agents. To guarantee control feasibility under actuator limitations, an auxiliary dynamic system (ADS) is introduced to suppress control inputs while preserving fixed-time convergence. Rigorous Lyapunov-based analysis establishes the closed-loop stability and provides an explicit, initial-condition-independent bound on the settling time. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed control scheme. Comparative studies further demonstrate that, in contrast to existing fixed-time controllers, the proposed approach improves tracking accuracy and ensures input constraint compliance, thereby enhancing robustness and practical implementability. To sum up, this distributed control scheme addresses the fixed-time coordination problem of NASs, enhancing cooperative control robustness in networked multiple quadrotors or large-scale robot groups in engineering applications for Industry 5.0.
Keywords: Uncertainty;Convergence;Fifth Industrial Revolution;Actuators;Robustness;Convex hulls;Protocols;Adaptive systems;Accuracy;Safety;Containment tracking;network agent systems;fixed-time convergence;lumped uncertainties;input saturation

Título: Startups in the Era of Industry 4.0 and 5.0: Technologies, Decisions, Framing, and Competences
Autores: Romano, André Luiz and Henrique Dos Santos, Carlos and Koch, Christoph and Lourenço Ubeda, Cristina and Rorato Fogaça, Diego and César Almada Santos, Fernando and Freitas, Vérica
Abstract: This article investigates the evolving domain of Startup 4.0/5.0, which leverages advanced Industry 4.0 and 5.0 technologies to support startups’ processes and activities. As startups face increasing complexity and competitiveness, understanding how digital innovations and emerging approaches contribute to improved performance, agility, and innovation becomes essential. Through a systematic literature review of peer-reviewed articles published up to December 2024, this study maps the current research landscape. The review responds to key research questions related to business sectors, applied tools, decision objectives, conceptual framings, and required skills and competences. Findings reveal a growing yet still underexplored field, with multidisciplinary relevance and a concentration of research in countries like Brazil and Germany, spanning sectors such as Advanced Manufacturing, Agrotech, Healthcare, and Education. Most reviewed works emphasize technical, managerial, and market-oriented perspectives, focusing on productivity and competitiveness, while elements central to Industry 5.0, such as sustainability, human-centric design, and resilience, remain marginal, appearing in few studies. Decision objectives were classified into key areas, including innovation, sustainability, digital transformation, and interinstitutional collaboration, highlighting the strategic role of digital technologies in business model redesign and ecosystem development. Moreover, the review identifies critical competences required for professionals in Startup 4.0/5.0 contexts, organizing several core competences into personal, social, and cultural categories and linking them to specific technologies, aiming to inform workforce training and behavioral change. By synthesizing these insights, the article contributes to a deeper theoretical understanding of Startup 4.0/5.0 and offers practical implications for this field.
Keywords: Fourth Industrial Revolution;Systematic literature review;Business;Fifth Industrial Revolution;Technological innovation;Resilience;Planning;Sustainable development;Ecosystems;Databases;Industry 4.0;Industry 5.0;startup;systematic literature review

Título: From Silos to Synergy: A Serious Game for Cross-Functional Collaboration in Human-Centric Asset Management
Autores: Barbieri, Giacomo and Zapata, Freddy
Abstract: Asset Management (AM) is an integrative discipline that relies on expert knowledge from diverse functions to develop holistic and coordinated solutions. However, the necessary division of responsibilities within and across organizations often leads to the formation of silos—isolated departments or teams that hinder communication and collaboration, ultimately undermining AM’s integrative nature. To address this challenge, a Serious Game (SG), From Silos to Synergy, was developed in this work. Guided by a Research through Design approach—where knowledge develops through iterative experimentation and the creation of artifacts—the SG aims to foster reflection on the relational and organizational dimensions of AM, thereby enabling the definition of cross-functional collaboration as a foundation of Human-Centric Asset Management (HuCAM). Grounded in a family finance analogy, the game integrates frameworks from AM, Industry 5.0, and game-based learning, underwent three design iterations, and was tested with 31 master’s students and 119 practitioners. The results indicate that the SG generated two main outcomes. On the one hand, it led to the creation of a Maturity Model for Cross-Functional Collaboration in HuCAM, offering a structured framework to evaluate and guide the transition toward more collaborative and human-centric AM practices. On the other hand, it fostered cultural awareness in cross-functional collaboration by challenging silo thinking and enhancing players’ understanding of the strategic and collaborative dimensions of AM. By promoting long-term value creation and human-centric thinking, From Silos to Synergy provides a practical and engaging pathway for developing the mindset and capabilities needed to tackle the complex, dynamic, and interdependent challenges of sustainability and resilience in modern asset systems.

Título: Rethinking Networked Robotics in the 6G Era With Generative AI-in-the-Loop
Autores: Li, Peizheng and Lin, Xinyi and Aijaz, Adnan
Abstract: Networked robotics continues to be a key component of various industrial systems. 6G will empower networked robotics with the envisaged capabilities like hyper-reliable and low-latency connectivity and in-network intelligence. While communication and control techniques have been widely investigated; co-design and AI-based solutions for autonomy and reasoning are still emerging. In this article, we propose a generative AI-in-the-Loop (GITL) framework for the control and coordination of networked robotic systems. The generative AI (GAI) agent oversees three interrelated loops: the communication loop, the robot control loop, and the AI model control loop, making holistic decisions by interpreting task requirements, network status, and robotic operations. Acting as a high-level cross-domain coordinator, the GAI agent leverages background knowledge of AI models, robot behaviors, and network policies, ensuring seamless interplay across different operational scenarios. This approach ultimately enables a highly autonomous networked robotic system capable of handling complex tasks with minimal human intervention. We anticipate that the GITL paradigm will play a pivotal role in unlocking the full potential of networked robotic systems, enabling enhanced autonomy, adaptability, and coordination in the emerging 6G and Industry 5.0 era.

Título: Domain Adaptation for Image Classification of Defects in Semiconductor Manufacturing
Autores: Poniatowski, Adrian and Gentner, Natalie and Barusco, Manuel and Pezze, Davide Dalle and Salti, Samuele and Susto, Gian Antonio
Jornal/Conferência: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
Abstract: In the semiconductor sector, due to high demand but also strong and increasing competition, time to market and quality are key factors in securing significant market share in various application areas. Thanks to the success of deep learning methods in recent years in the computer vision domain, Industry 4.0 and 5.0 applications, such as defect classification, have achieved remarkable success. In particular, Domain Adaptation (DA) has proven highly effective since it focuses on using the knowledge learned on a (source) domain to adapt and perform effectively on a different but related (target) domain. By improving robustness and scalability, DA minimizes the need for extensive manual re-labeling or retraining of models. This not only reduces computational and resource costs but also allows human experts to focus on high-value tasks. Therefore, we tested the efficacy of DA techniques in semi-supervised and unsupervised settings within the context of the semiconductor field. Moreover, we propose the DBACS approach, a CycleGAN-inspired model enhanced with additional loss terms to improve performance. All the approaches are studied and validated on real-world Electron Microscope images, considering the unsupervised and semi-supervised settings, proving the usefulness of our method in advancing DA techniques for the semiconductor field.

Título: Future Factories with 6G: Agentic AI and Cyber-Physical Digital Twins
Autores: Li, Haiyuan and Madhukumar, Hari and Methley, Nicholas and Chen, Xuewen and Wu, Yulei and Parra-Ullauri, Juan and Sharma, Vishnu and Lee, Jeongran and Koblitz, Arndt Ryo and Andrews, Matthew and Liu, Sige and Deng, Yansha and Kolawole, Oluwatayo Y. and Tassi, Andrea and Simeonidou, Dimitra
Abstract: Industry 5.0 envisions a cyber-physical future where humans and robots collaborate harmoniously, empowered by 6G connectivity and intelligent automation. Central to this vision is the ability to autonomously configure complex production pipelines based on diverse and evolving human intents. Existing orchestration technologies exhibit critical shortcomings in terms of self-learning, validation, error diagnosis, and rectification capabilities. To this end, we propose an Agentic AI orchestration framework that interprets human intents and dynamically assembles optimal technology pipelines using a self-improving, retrieval-augmented Large Language Model (LLM) and a Bayesian contextual-bandit selector. This enables dynamic adaptation in unpredictable factory environments. Our solution is validated in a cyber-physical testbed integrating Digital Twins (DTs), distributed AI, robotics, and real-world network infrastructure. Compared to baseline LLMs, our system reduces orchestration iterations by over 94% for a given intent and by around 90% for an unseen intent, showing rapid convergence and strong generalization. Real-world deployments mirror DT results, confirming both the fidelity of the simulation and the practical value of intent-driven orchestration for human-centric manufacturing.

Título: Optimizing Multitask Industrial Processes With Predictive Action Guidance
Autores: Mehta, Naval Kishore and Arvind and Prasad, Shyam Sunder and Saurav, Sumeet and Singh, Sanjay
Jornal/Conferência: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
Abstract: Monitoring complex assembly processes is critical for maintaining productivity and ensuring compliance with assembly standards. However, variability in human actions and subjective task preferences complicate accurate task anticipation and guidance. To address these challenges, we introduce the Multi-Modal Transformer Fusion and Recurrent Units (MMTF-RU) Network for egocentric activity anticipation, utilizing multi-modal fusion to improve prediction accuracy. Integrated with the Operator Action Monitoring Unit (OAMU), the system provides proactive operator guidance, preventing deviations in the assembly process. OAMU employs two strategies: 1) Top-5 MMTF-RU predictions, combined with a reference graph and an action dictionary, for next-step recommendations and 2) Top-1 MMTF-RU predictions, integrated with a reference graph, for detecting sequence deviations and predicting anomaly scores via an entropy-informed confidence mechanism. We also introduce Time-Weighted Sequence Accuracy (TWSA) to evaluate operator efficiency and ensure timely task completion. Our approach is validated on the industrial Meccano dataset and the large-scale EPIC-Kitchens-55 dataset, demonstrating its effectiveness in dynamic environments. Note to Practitioners—Manual assembly remains crucial in industries that require human dexterity and adaptability for tasks that are too complex, customized, or low-volume for full automation. We propose a system to enhance the accuracy of these processes by predicting operator actions and providing real-time guidance through multi-modal data. Its primary function is to ensure that tasks are completed in the correct sequence, thereby reducing human error and boosting productivity. The system is particularly suited for industries like automotive and electronics manufacturing, where precision and flexibility are critical to maintaining high product quality. In addition to providing real-time feedback, the system continuously monitors the sequence and timing of operator actions using multi-modal data. It detects anomalies such as delays, repeated attempts, or missed steps, flags them as bottlenecks, and provides immediate corrective guidance. Such functionality helps operators stay aligned with the expected task flow, minimizes inefficiencies, and reduces cycle time, thereby reducing the need for corrective measures and post-process inspections while delivering immediate operational benefits. This solution offers significant potential for transforming manual assembly workflows, improving accuracy, efficiency, and consistency, while proactively addressing inefficiencies. It represents a key step toward creating smarter, human-centric manufacturing environments that align with the goals of Industry 5.0.

Título: An Improved Hybrid Approach for Proactive Healthcare Industry Risk Prediction: Integrating Graph Weighted Fusion, RF and RW-GCN
Autores: Bi, KeJun and Liu, ChuanJie and Dai, Cheng and Guo, Bing and Politis, Ilias
Jornal/Conferência: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics
Abstract: Risk prediction in healthcare industrial chains is critical for ensuring operational resilience and systemic stability. Traditional methods often focus on supply chain topology while overlooking enterprise-level indicators and the complex interdependencies among participants. To address these limitations, we propose IA-GWRG, a hybrid framework that integrates multi-relational graph modeling, key indicator selection, and subgraph-level learning for fine-grained enterprise risk prediction. Designed to align with emerging 6G-enabled intelligent infrastructures, IA-GWRG leverages ultra-low latency and ubiquitous sensing to enable real-time risk awareness. First, we introduce a salient graph feature extraction method that transforms a multi-relational industrial chain graph into a homogeneous structure using weighted fusion based on “competition–supply” meta-paths. A local-global-positional scheme is then applied to capture multi-scale structural features. Second, a key indicator identification module constructs a domain-specific 26-dimensional risk system and employs a random forest algorithm to select the most informative micro-level indicators, enhancing interpretability and reducing feature noise. Third, a node risk assessment method combines selected indicators and structural embeddings via subgraph-level random walk sampling and GCN-based learning, enabling precise and context-aware risk prediction. Extensive experiments on real-world healthcare industry chain datasets demonstrate that IA-GWRG consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across multiple metrics. The results confirm its effectiveness and robustness in both predictive accuracy and 6G-oriented deployment scenarios.
Keywords: Medical services;Feature extraction;Random forests;Risk management;Supply chains;Industries;6G mobile communication;Real-time systems;Graph neural networks;Bioinformatics;Healthcare Industry 5.0;Risk assessment;Heterogeneous graph;Graph neural network (GNN);Random forest;Meta-path;Industrial chain resilience

Título: The Role of Photonic Sensing Technologies in Healthcare 5.0: A Comprehensive Review of Future Perspectives and Applications
Autores: Leal-Junior, Arnaldo and Nedoma, Jan and Martinek, Radek
Abstract: This article presents a review of Healthcare 5.0 and its historical perspective, considering the industrial revolutions. The main aspects and challenges of the next generation of healthcare systems are discussed. Due to the inherent advantages of optical fiber sensor (OFS) systems, such technology is comprehensively reviewed and discussed in terms of healthcare applications. Thereafter, an analytical correlation is performed between OFS technologies and the requirements of Healthcare 5.0, and discussed in detail. The key parameters in Healthcare 5.0 indicated that OFS technology aligns well with the requirements and challenges of Healthcare 5.0. Thus, photonic technologies play a key role in the future of healthcare, especially in innovative approaches for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), as such approaches are readily available for use with optical fibers that combine excellent signal transmission and distributed sensing capabilities. Thus, the contributions of this work are related to the first review of Healthcare 5.0, focused on the role of photonic technologies in such new healthcare evolution, as well as the analysis concerning the key aspects of such applications.

Título: Automation–Augmentation Entanglement: Self-Service-Technology as Driver for Change
Autores: Altrock, Sophie and Mention, Anne-Laure and Aas, Tor Helge
Abstract: Although the automation of work is not new, advancements in artificial intelligence, worker shortages, and the Covid-19 pandemic have accelerated recent debates. Especially in service sectors, traditional service delivery is gradually merging with machine components, requiring organizations to rethink models of service delivery. Since the adoption of self-service technology (SST) grows, users benefit from improved access and self-management without human touchpoint, yet the impact of SST on workers requires further exploration. While technology-enabled workplace transformation is well researched, unified frameworks and strategies are missing to understand the interplay of augmentation and automation as SST becomes a ubiquitous component of service. Through an integrative review we explore most cited and most recent literature on automation, augmentation, and SST. In total, we review 41 articles. This review provides a status quo on the topics automation, augmentation, and SST. Providing a combined lens, five emerging themes are discovered for future research: Social (A)symmetries, Competing Intelligences, Redistributed Responsibilities and New Skills, Merging Spaces and New Ecosystems, Governance and Ethics. This article provides an interdisciplinary review of service automation, extends previous scholarly work, and encourages new pathways for hybrid service delivery. Furthermore, embedded in the concept of a human-centered Industry 5.0, we suggest automation–augmentation entanglement as holistic framework reflecting the interplay of human and technology in the workplace.

Título: Improved Carnivorous Plant Algorithm for Human–Robot Collaborative U-Shaped Disassembly Line Balancing With Mobile Workers
Autores: Qin, Shujin and Dai, Shaokang and Wang, Jiacun and Liu, Shixin and Guo, Xiwang and Qi, Liang and Hu, Bin and Ji, Yingjun
Jornal/Conferência: IEEE Transactions on Computational Social Systems
Abstract: The advancement of human–robot collaboration technology has positioned remanufacturing as a crucial part of the circular economy, driving both economic growth and environmental sustainability. In the era of Industry 5.0, these technologies enhance the efficiency and flexibility of disassembly tasks. However, most research on human–robot collaborative disassembly (HRCD) line balancing overlooks the mobility of workers. This study introduces a profit-oriented HRCD model incorporating mobile workers. To address large-scale HRCD challenges, it proposes a dynamic attraction rate mechanism that improves the traditional carnivorous plant algorithm (CPA), tackling issues of slow convergence and local optimization. The experimental framework includes three validation phases: 1) comparison with the exact solver IBM ILOG CPLEX Optimization Studio (CPLEX); 2) parameter sensitivity analysis; and 3) benchmarking against seven state-of-the-art algorithms. Results demonstrate that HRCD with mobile workers significantly boosts disassembly efficiency and reduces disassembly time compared to traditional methods. Additionally, it increases profits through flexible task allocation. In cases of incomplete disassembly, HRCD with mobile workers yields an average benefit increase of 87.64% over conventional disassembly modes. A comparative evaluation with other swarm intelligence algorithms further highlights the superior solution quality and time efficiency of the improved CPA.

Título: Scientific mapping and systematic literature review on socio-technical change and transition to Industry 5.0 or Society 5.0
Autores: Hernández, Iván Manuel De la Vega and Sekli, Giulio Marchena and Santander, Kelly
Abstract: The purpose of this study is to explore two of the main currents of thought on the evolution of humanity, derived from the great transformations driven by technological change. The purpose is to recognize the characteristics, similarities and differences, of the Industry 5.0 (I5.0) and Society 5.0 (S5.0) models and to propose scenarios with distinctive features to determine which of them will prevail in the future. The approach of the study is deductive, the strategy is exploratory and the method applied is mixed. The quantitative method was developed through a longitudinal scientific mapping performed in WoS and Scopus databases. The qualitative method was carried out through an exhaustive review of the literature using terminology connected to the topics explored. This mapping made it possible to identify the countries, institutions, scientific collaboration networks and leading authors in these fields of knowledge. The results revealed convergent and divergent attributes between the two approaches. There is a set of technologies that will predictably prevail, regardless of the model adopted. However, key differences in the approaches and in the dynamics of human-technology interaction were also identified. It is assumed that both models are complementary in the use of technologies, but their fundamental difference lies in the approach. Industry 5.0 focuses on the sphere of high-end manufacturing, with an emphasis on enhancing human creativity and labor welfare through technological integration, while Society 5.0 prioritizes a broad social spectrum and integrates various aspects of life where there is an intelligent audit of the use of technology.
Keywords: Fifth Industrial Revolution;Biological system modeling;Pandemics;Systematic literature review;Socioeconomics;Organizations;Industries;Fourth Industrial Revolution;Technological innovation;Sustainable development;Industry 5.0;Society 5.0;explanatory models;scenarios;socio-technical change

Título: A Survey on Security and Privacy of Industry 4.0 and Beyond: Technical Aspects, Use Cases, Challenges, and Research Directions
Autores: Singh Gaba, Gurjot and Sari, Alparslan and Butun, Ismail and Singh, Parminder and Gurtov, Andrei and Liyanage, Madhusanka
Jornal/Conferência: IEEE Open Journal of the Communications Society
Abstract: Industry 4.0 and 5.0 offer a promising framework for connecting electro-mechanical systems to cyberspace, enabling real-time access, telecontrol, human-machine collaboration, and intelligent automation of industrial operations. While horizontal and vertical interoperability serve as critical enablers of this ecosystem, heterogeneity among entities and the lack of standardized governance in interoperability allow cybercriminals to exploit structural vulnerabilities. These weaknesses and unknown bugs provide avenues for cyber-attackers to breach systems, conduct espionage, sabotage assets, and extort organizations, threatening IT and OT infrastructures, finances, reputations, and even human lives. This survey paper discusses cybersecurity and privacy threats within the Industry 4.0 and 5.0 ecosystems, their potential impact on industrial processes and peripherals, and the security challenges associated with the transition from Industry 4.0 to 5.0. To identify research gaps and vulnerabilities, we examine the architecture and components of diverse industrial frameworks and establish functional mappings using IIRA and RAMI models. Following a comprehensive threat modeling approach, we present a layered taxonomy of cyber-threats, classified based on their nature, behavior, and execution characteristics. To assist network administrators and security professionals, we propose a threat prioritization framework based on likelihood, detectability, impact severity, and operational consequences. Furthermore, we outline perspective-based cybersecurity challenges that expose deficiencies in current protective measures. As countermeasures, we advocate for AI-driven, blockchain-enabled, edge-computing-based, and privacy-preserving security solutions to defend against threats and mitigate potential damages. We also elaborate on key standardization initiatives, nation-specific privacy regulations, and ongoing research efforts focused on safeguarding the security and privacy of Industry 4.0 and beyond. The paper concludes by summarizing key lessons learned, identifying unresolved research questions, and suggesting future directions for a secure and resilient Industry 5.0 paradigm.
Keywords: Fourth Industrial Revolution;Security;Industries;Computer security;Fifth Industrial Revolution;Cyberattack;Artificial intelligence;Privacy;Universal Serial Bus;Real-time systems;Cybersecurity;cyber-physical systems (CPS);Industry 4.0;industrial Internet;privacy

Título: Boosting Trustworthiness in 6G-Enabled Smart Industries 5.0 through Explainable Artificial Intelligence on Industrial Machine Anomaly Data
Autores: Jing, Hengchang and Huang, Lijia
Abstract: New industrial paradigms, like Industry 5.0 and the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), are developing in industrial contexts with the objective of foster quality. The growth of 6G-enabled smart industries requires interpretable, secure, and adaptive anomaly detection structures able to operate under adversarial, dynamic, and resource-constrained environments. Inappropriately, the usage of these technologies, successively, strengthens the attacking surface and poses a significant attack to the novel goals of Industry 5.0, like enhancing the user experience, resilience, and sustainability. In this setting, human-machine collaboration and cyber-physical integration request that anomaly detection systems surpass only prediction and include resilience, interpretability, and scalability. Traditional anomaly detection systems in Industry 4.0, like machine learning (ML)-based detection show remarkable challenges. These contain vulnerability to antagonistic attacks owing to vulnerable updates of the model, rigidity in adjusting to concept and temporal drift, and unclear decision processes that hamper trust and accountability. Therefore, this study develops an explainable artificial intelligence with a feature selection strategy enabled anomaly detection (XAIFSS-AD) technique for improving trustworthiness in 6G driven smart industry 5.0. The primary objective is to unravel the security issues in the smart industry environment via the anomaly identification process with the XAI approach to elaborate the proposed model. The presented XAIFSS-AD technique involves data scaling using a robust scalar which uses median and interquartile range to standardize the network data. In addition, the selection of features can be performed using the recursive feature elimination (RFE) process to eliminate the least significant features and enhance the classification process. A variational autoencoder with attention bidirectional long short-term memory (VAE-ABiLSTM) is deployed for anomaly detection. The performance of the classification model can be fine-tuned by Tree-structured Parzen Estimator (TPE) which optimally chooses the hyperparameter values. Finally, the Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME) methodology is applied to offer descriptions of the presented methods. The performance of the XAIFSS-AD approach is evaluated utilizing the benchmark datasets. The outcomes specify that the proposed model surpasses the other inspected systems and advanced models.

Título: Co-Designed Proactive–Reactive Composite Defense and IT2-Type Fuzzy Control for Active Vehicle Suspensions Systems: Theory and Experiment
Autores: Du, Mengni and Xie, Xiang-Peng
Abstract: Under the background of Industry 5.0, the integration of cyber-physical systems into industrial operations has exposed security vulnerabilities stemming from insufficient security strategies. To address the nonlinear characteristics and network security problems in active vehicle suspension systems (AVSSs), a cooperative control strategy combining interval type-2 (IT2) fuzzy control and moving target defense (MTD) is proposed. First, a discrete-time IT2 fuzzy-based suspension model is developed under sophisticated false data injection (FDI) attacks, incorporating parameter perturbations. Second, in order to counter sophisticated FDI attackers with system knowledge, the proactive–reactive composite defense (PRCD) mechanism is designed. The proactive layer constructs the dynamic system by parameter switching based on the MTD, and the reactive layer constructs the residual detection model using the observer. The PRCD mechanism prevents attacker reconnaissance, enhances defensive capability, and enables attack detection. Third, a switching multimode gain-scheduling control law is proposed based on the homogeneous polynomial technique in the proactive layer. At the same time, a group of augmented time-varying reciprocal matrices is constructed for each switching mode. These matrices are integrated into the stability analysis of the AVSSs to reduce conservatism. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is confirmed through hardware-in-the-loop experiments.

Título: Copper and Aluminum Scrap Detection Model Based on Improved YOLOv11n
Autores: Huang, Bo and Zhou, Chongshan and Wu, Junqi and Liu, Jun and Yan, Yang
Abstract: With the development of global industry, the recycling of waste copper and aluminium metals from end-of-life vehicles holds significant economic and environmental value. Machine vision technology plays a crucial role in scrap metal recycling, where accurate identification of waste metals has consistently been a key focus in this field. To address issues such as missed detections, false positives, and low detection accuracy caused by complex backgrounds in copper and aluminium scrap detection, along with the need for lightweight deployment, an improved YOLOv11n-based detection model for copper and aluminium scraps is proposed. The C3k2_Star_CAA module was designed to replace the original C3K2 module, improving feature extraction and target recognition in complex environments. The FPNSC module was introduced in place of the original SPPF module to capture finer features while keeping the model lightweight. A Feature Focus Diffusion Pyramid Network (FDPN) was adopted to substitute the original feature pyramid network, enhancing multi-scale feature fusion through FocusFeature modules and a diffusion mechanism. Additionally, a Dynamic Detection Head (DyHead) was incorporated to replace the original detection head, integrating multi-scale features to improve detection accuracy for objects of different sizes. Experimental results demonstrate that the improved model achieved a 9% increase in mAP@0.5, a 6.5% improvement in mAP@0.5:0.95, along with 3.9% higher Precision, 12.4% better Recall, and 8.2% greater F1-Score on the dataset, while also showing significant improvements in both parameter count and detection speed, making it more suitable for copper and aluminium scrap detection tasks. Furthermore, generalisation experiments using public datasets confirmed that the model exhibits strong generalisation capabilities.
